'''Jens Franke''' (born 28 June 1964) is a German mathematician. He has held a chair at the [[University of Bonn]]'s [[Hausdorff Center for Mathematics]] since 1992. Franke's research has covered various problems of [[number theory]], [[algebraic geometry]] and [[analysis]] on locally symmetric spaces.

Franke attended the [[University of Jena]], where he earned his PhD under [[Hans Triebel]] in 1986. He was awarded the [[EMS Prize]] in 1992, and the [[Oberwolfach Prize]] in 1993.

In recent years, Franke worked on an implementation of the [[Number Field Sieve]] algorithm for [[prime decomposition]]. In May 2007, he and his colleague [[Thorsten Kleinjung]] announced the factorization of ''M''<sub>1039</sub>, the 1,039th [[Mersenne number]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.crypto-world.com/announcements/m1039.txt |title=Archived copy |access-date=2010-05-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150222214158/http://www.crypto-world.com/announcements/m1039.txt |archive-date=2015-02-22 |url-status=dead }} {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190711041600/http://www.crypto-world.com/announcements/m1039.txt |date=2019-07-11 }}</ref>
